correctness.rationale: For each rank-j frequency the rank-one sphere transform is evaluated by exact outer-product orthogonality and its rank-two counterpart follows from complete character orthogonality. The three kernel multipliers are then explicit and the only potentially negative one is \(f(z)=1-(q+1)z+qz^{2^\alpha}\). Strict convexity proves the unique interior transition iff \(2^\alpha>1+1/q\). The CND Fourier multipliers prove the exact endpoint and nullity. Independent geometric proof: the sharp powered metric is 1/q times the sum of projective-line Hamming mismatches; regular simplices attain minimal Euclidean dimension N1, while Fourier rank proves minimality. Finite raw-character enumeration in the actual package passed at \((q,m)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3),(4,2)\); this is corroboration, not the universal proof. Boundary t=0 and \(m\ge2\) explicitly handled.

value.rationale: The two-column full rank-metric space is a canonical infinite family of diameter-two bilinear-forms graphs. Identifying the exact maximal negative-type exponent establishes precisely when Gaussian kernels are valid at every scale and yields the unique sharp bandwidth threshold for every larger exponent. The rank-two-only degeneracy and abrupt optimal Hilbert embedding dimension drop are structural, and the projective-line Hamming factorization gives an explicit geometric realization. Uniformity in both finite-field size and number of matrix rows makes this a motivated complete phase classification rather than a routine finite table.
